inputCoverage.agencyScope: Complete features intersecting input window from existing source cache; not a fresh agency census

recommendation.summary: Review a segment-level merge: keep one overlapping alignment and verify the outlying sections as possible unique ends or branches. Do not connect them automatically.
reasons: OpenStreetMap: 56% of its geometry lies within 15 m of the other source; 60% within 50 m. Median nearest-line offset 5.5 m.
NPS: 94% of its geometry lies within 15 m of the other source; 98% within 50 m. Median nearest-line offset 1.6 m.

Within the same input window, OpenStreetMap: 34,317 m long, median vertex spacing 22.3 m, 13,704 m outside the other source’s 50 m corridor; NPS: 19,887 m long, median vertex spacing 18.3 m, 408 m outside the other source’s 50 m corridor.

Endpoint check: OpenStreetMap has 177 non-seam endpoint candidates over 75 m from the other alignment; NPS has 2 non-seam endpoint candidates over 75 m from the other alignment. These can be real additions, branches, or source gaps; inspect their connections.

DEM sanity check in the shared corridor: OpenStreetMap: 90th-percentile absolute terrain grade 7.8% over 281 sampled 50 m sections; NPS: 90th-percentile absolute terrain grade 8.2% over 287 sampled 50 m sections. Lower grade alone does not mean a route is more accurate.
Vertex density measures representation detail, not survey accuracy. Sharp turns may be genuine switchbacks; geometry alone cannot diagnose GPS multipath.
recommendation.limitations: Heuristic guidance, not an independent ground-truth verdict. Uses source geometry and frozen DEM only; no imagery interpretation or route editing. DEM measures ground surface, not surveyed trail elevation. Full agency inputs and OSM tile fragments have different lineage; no automatic edits.
